cells.note: Orphan path works in-session (footnote.ts:188-214 dispatches virgil-footnote-orphaned; footnote-sync.ts:40-48 mirrors into orphanedFootnotes; OrphanedFootnoteCard renders with BadgeOrphaned + no jump). BUT empty-bodied footnotes are silently dropped (footnote.ts:204 gates on non-empty plain text), and orphans first/anchored second concat (FootnotePanel.tsx:114-121) has no de-dup. The reconciler pruner can never clear a stale cardStore ref for a deleted footnote (useAnchorHighlightReconciler.ts:84-90, isInlineAtomCardKind ⇒ entityExists=true).

orphanedFootnotes is ephemeral React state in EditorLayout (EditorLayout.tsx:1106), never read from or written to any sidecar (useFootnotes.syncFromEditor is NEVER called for footnotes — only citationsHook.syncFromEditor at EditorPane.tsx:1180). Orphan content is lost on reload. Title + thanks are dropped at orphaning (footnote.ts:208 detail carries only {footnoteId, content}). No reset on doc switch → cross-doc orphan leak.

Footnote atoms are their own anchors, so two cards can't statically share an anchor. BUT the orphan re-drop window (Editor.tsx:753 inserts atom synchronously, virgil-footnote-panel-dropped fires via setTimeout(0) at :755) leaves the panel rendering BOTH the freshly-anchored footnote AND the still-present orphan with the SAME footnoteId — React key collision (CardListPanel.tsx:143 Fragment key=id) + identical data-card-key.

Docked↔omni↔float selection sync is unified through cardStore (setSelectedFootnoteId === makeKindSetter('footnote') routes to cardStore.select; selections.tsx:124,201) — PASS for selection. Footnote ids are stable (not regenerated like citations), so pin store (omni-pin-store.ts) keys hold — lead #3 N-A for footnotes. BUG: popping out a footnote then orphaning it (delete marker) makes FloatHost render null (FloatHost.tsx:44-45 via floats/index.tsx:218-220 getFootnotes().find ⇒ undefined) but the key stays in poppedOutCards — float silently vanishes, content stranded in the un-floatable orphan card. Sidecar (footnotes.json) is vestigial for anchored footnotes (content lives in node attrs/.tex).

Generic panel toggle/reorder/collapse/split go through the shared system (panel-registry.ts:59-67 omniEligible:true, omniSide:left) — PASS. BUG: count badge = footnotes.length (anchored only, FootnotePanel.tsx:132) but items[] includes orphans (FootnotePanel.tsx:114-121). With orphans present the badge undercounts (or shows nothing at count=0, PanelHeader hides it at panel-primitives.tsx:2088). Citations (orderedCitations.length, includes unanchored) and Reports (cards.length) count correctly — footnotes is the outlier.

findings.subject: footnotes
findings.symptom: An orphaned footnote (marker deleted in-text, content recoverable in the panel) vanishes permanently on document reload or doc switch — the recovery affordance only survives within the live session.
findings.suspectedRootCause: orphanedFootnotes is a plain useState([]) in EditorLayout (EditorLayout.tsx:1106) that is never serialized to any sidecar. useFootnotes owns footnotes.json and exposes syncFromEditor, but EditorPane never calls footnotesHook.syncFromEditor (only citationsHook.syncFromEditor at EditorPane.tsx:1180) and createFootnote never calls footnotesHook.addFootnote (card-creation.ts:516-554), so the footnote sidecar is effectively never populated. When the marker is deleted the \footnote{} text is already gone from the .tex, so the orphan's content lives ONLY in ephemeral React state. No persistence path exists.

evidence.note: const [orphanedFootnotes, setOrphanedFootnotes] = useState<OrphanedFootnote[]>([]) — ephemeral, never hydrated from disk
all orphan handlers mutate React state only; no writeSidecar anywhere
syncFromEditor (the only path that would persist unanchored footnotes) exists but is never invoked for footnotes
only citationsHook.syncFromEditor is called on editor mount; the footnote equivalent is absent

reproSteps: Open a paper with a footnote that has prose content
Delete the footnote's superscript marker in the main text (backspace over it)
Observe the orphaned-footnote card appears in the Footnotes panel with its content intact
Reload the document (or switch to another doc and back)
The orphaned footnote — and its content — is gone with no warning
findings.suspectedClass: Any panel state held at the EditorLayout shell level (vs a sidecar-backed per-doc hook) shares this loss-on-reload + leak-on-doc-switch risk. Orphan/transient-recovery collections that are not persisted are the class.

findings.subject: footnotes
findings.symptom: When a footnote that has a user-authored title (or is a \thanks acknowledgement) is orphaned, the title and the acknowledgement identity are silently dropped — the orphan card shows an empty +T title and a generic orphan badge instead of the 'A' acknowledgement badge.
findings.suspectedRootCause: The orphan-detector builds the virgil-footnote-orphaned event detail with only {footnoteId, content} (footnote.ts:208), discarding oldNode.attrs.title and oldNode.attrs.thanks even though OrphanedFootnote has a title field (types.ts:568) and the anchored card renders a 'Acknowledgement'/'A' identity from fn.thanks (FootnoteCard.tsx:116,122). The orphan record therefore never receives the title/thanks.

evidence.note: detail: { footnoteId: removed.id, content } — title and thanks attrs are not read or forwarded
OrphanedFootnote.title?: string — the slot exists but is never populated by the detector
anchored card derives 'Acknowledgement' label + 'A' badge from fn.thanks — lost when orphaned (OrphanedFootnoteCard always renders BadgeOrphaned)

reproSteps: Create a footnote, give it a title via the +T affordance (or make it a \thanks acknowledgement)
Delete its marker in the main text
Observe the orphan card has no title (+T placeholder) and a plain orphan dot — the title/acknowledgement identity is gone even before reload
findings.suspectedClass: Any teardown→recovery event that reconstructs a record from a subset of the source node's attrs. The detector pulls content but not the full attr set; the same omission would affect any future per-footnote attr (e.g. a future kind discriminator).

findings.subject: footnotes
findings.symptom: Orphaned footnotes from one document persist into a different document's Footnotes panel after switching docs — orphans with footnoteIds that belong to the previous paper appear (and can't jump, can't re-anchor meaningfully) in the new paper's panel.
findings.suspectedRootCause: orphanedFootnotes lives in EditorLayout (the multi-doc shell, EditorLayout.tsx:1106) which is not remounted per doc (EditorPane is the per-doc owner). No effect resets orphanedFootnotes on docId change (grep confirms only setter calls are the bridge handlers). So the orphan list accumulates across the session and across doc switches.

evidence.note: shell-level state with no docId-keyed reset effect
the only producer just appends; nothing clears on doc switch

reproSteps: In doc A, orphan a footnote (delete its marker) so an orphan card appears
Switch to doc B (different paper) without reloading
Observe doc B's Footnotes panel shows doc A's orphan footnote
findings.suspectedClass: Any shell-level (EditorLayout) state that should be per-doc but isn't reset on docId change. Companion to the suppressOrphanRef latch which is also shell-level and never reset.

findings.subject: footnotes
findings.symptom: A deleted footnote can leave a stale selection/expansion/hover reference in the global cardStore that is never pruned, so the selection slot keeps pointing at a footnote that no longer exists anywhere (no atom, no orphan, no sidecar).
findings.suspectedRootCause: The dangling-ref pruner exempts inline-atom kinds: entityExists() returns true unconditionally for footnote/citation (useAnchorHighlightReconciler.ts:84-90 via isInlineAtomCardKind), so when a footnote is hard-deleted (trash on card → handleDeleteFootnote, which suppresses the orphan) the pruner at :157-165 can never clear cardStore.selected / hover / expandedSet entries for it. The reconciler then resolves the link to no DOM (findInlineAtomPos returns null) so nothing visibly paints, but selectedFootnoteId (derived from the store) reports a ghost id until the user selects another card or clicks away.

evidence.note: if (isInlineAtomCardKind(ref.kind)) return true — footnote refs are treated as always-present, defeating the pruner
the prune block calls entityExists and so never clears a deleted footnote's selection/hover/expansion
handleDeleteFootnote removes the atom and arms the suppress latch — no cardStore.clearSelection for the deleted id

reproSteps: Select a footnote card (halo on)
Delete it via the card's trash button
cardStore.selected still holds {kind:'footnote', id} (now non-existent); the derived selectedFootnoteId is a ghost until the next select/click-away
Equivalent: hover a footnote card then delete it — cardStore.hover is not pruned
findings.suspectedClass: Lead #2: the inline-atom exemption affects BOTH footnotes and citations identically — a deleted citation has the same stale-ghost-ref risk. Any kind the pruner can't classify is exempt.

findings.subject: footnotes
findings.symptom: Deleting the marker of a footnote whose body is empty (e.g. a title-only footnote, or a freshly-created blank one the user titled) produces NO orphan card — the footnote and any title silently disappear with no recovery affordance.
findings.suspectedRootCause: The orphan-detector only dispatches virgil-footnote-orphaned when richJsonToPlainText(content).trim() is non-empty (footnote.ts:204). A footnote with an empty body but a non-empty title still fails this gate, so it is never orphaned and its title is lost (compounds FN-A2-02).

evidence.note: if (content && richJsonToPlainText(content).trim()) — title-only / empty-body footnotes skip orphan creation entirely

reproSteps: Create a footnote, give it a title but leave the body empty
Delete its marker in text
No orphan card appears; the title is gone
findings.suspectedClass: Content-emptiness gates that ignore non-body fields (title/metadata). The has-content predicate family (cardHasContent / hasJsonContent) similarly considers only body content for footnotes — see the F7 lead #1.

findings.subject: footnotes
findings.symptom: During an orphan re-drop, the Footnotes panel briefly renders two cards with the SAME footnoteId — the freshly re-anchored footnote and the not-yet-removed orphan — causing a React key collision and a one-frame duplicate (both share the same data-card-key, so a halo would paint both).
findings.suspectedRootCause: The re-drop inserts the new footnote atom synchronously (Editor.tsx:752-753 view.dispatch) which immediately bumps rev.footnotes and re-derives footnoteInfos, but the orphan is only removed when the deferred virgil-footnote-panel-dropped fires via setTimeout(0) (Editor.tsx:755-761). FootnotePanel.items concatenates orphanedFootnotes + footnotes with no de-dup by id (FootnotePanel.tsx:114-121), and the omni builder does the same (omni.tsx:30-82). CardListPanel keys each item by footnoteId (CardListPanel.tsx:143).

evidence.note: synchronous tr.insert of the re-dropped footnote atom
setTimeout(0) before dispatching virgil-footnote-panel-dropped that removes the orphan — opens the duplicate window
items = [...orphanedFootnotes, ...footnotes] with getId = footnoteId for both; no de-dup → React key collision when an id is in both lists

reproSteps: Orphan a footnote (delete its marker)
Drag the orphan card back into the document text
For one render cycle the panel shows both an anchored and an orphan card with the same id (React key-collision warning in console)
findings.suspectedClass: Any two lists merged by id without a de-dup pass while one list is updated synchronously and the other via a deferred event. The orphan↔anchored seam is the canonical instance.

findings.subject: footnotes
findings.symptom: If a footnote is popped out into a floating window and then orphaned (its marker deleted in text), the float window silently disappears and its key is leaked in poppedOutCards; the (still-recoverable) content is stranded in the docked orphan card, which has no popout affordance.
findings.suspectedRootCause: The footnote Floatable resolves its data from the live editor (floats/index.tsx:218-220 getFootnotes().find) and returns null when the atom is gone. FloatHost renders null for that key (FloatHost.tsx:44-45) but never removes it from poppedOutCards / prefs. There is no orphan-footnote Floatable registration, and no migration of the float to the orphan record on orphaning.

evidence.note: liveFootnotes = getFootnotes(); fn = find(id); if (!fn) return null — orphaned footnote yields no float body
resolveFloatable returns null ⇒ FloatHost renders nothing, but the key persists in keys/poppedOutCards
orphaning path adds the orphan but does not close/remap any open float for that footnote

reproSteps: Pop out a footnote card into a floating window
Delete the footnote's marker in the main text (orphaning it)
The float window vanishes with no explanation; the orphan card appears docked but cannot be re-popped; the float key remains in prefs
findings.suspectedClass: Float keys whose underlying entity can transition to a state with no Floatable resolver (orphan footnote, deleted citation) leak in poppedOutCards. Any kind without a defensive 'close float on entity disappearance' is in the class.

findings.subject: footnotes
findings.symptom: The Footnotes panel header count badge undercounts when orphaned footnotes are present — it shows only the anchored count (and shows nothing at all when there are 0 anchored + N orphans), while the panel body renders N more cards than the badge claims.
findings.suspectedRootCause: FootnotePanel passes count={footnotes.length} (anchored only, FootnotePanel.tsx:132) but builds items from [...orphanedFootnotes, ...footnotes] (FootnotePanel.tsx:114-121). PanelHeader hides the badge entirely when count <= 0 (panel-primitives.tsx:2088). By contrast Citations counts orderedCitations.length (includes unanchored drafts) and Reports counts cards.length — footnotes is the only left card panel that excludes its unanchored/orphan items from the count.

evidence.note: count={footnotes.length} — orphans excluded
items include orphans first, then anchored — rendered count diverges from badge count
{count != null && count > 0 && ...} — badge hidden at 0, so 0-anchored+N-orphan reads as no badge
count={orderedCitations.length} includes unanchored — establishes the inconsistency

reproSteps: Have a paper with 2 anchored footnotes and 1 orphan
Observe the Footnotes panel badge reads '2' while 3 cards render
Delete the markers of all anchored footnotes so only orphans remain — the badge disappears entirely while orphan cards still render
findings.suspectedClass: Panels with a separate orphan/unanchored sub-list passing only the anchored count to the badge. Footnotes is the outlier vs Citations/Reports — the class is 'badge count derived from a narrower list than items'.
